report:
Reviewed the complete precedence claim, seven ordinary implementation associations, and all 23 associated test entries (22 executable behavior tests and the explicit TODO). This is partial coverage, not a claim of complete Rust name-resolution conformance.

Implementation: resolve/mod.rs gives ribs priority for unqualified one-segment paths, resolves longer paths through Type namespace containers, distinguishes anchored self/super/crate/external paths, and searches named items before globs in normal mode, followed by external/edition/language preludes. MacroExpansion mode deliberately retains combined named/glob lookup. Lookup tracks module/name/namespace recursion and deduplicates definition identity after selecting a precedence bucket; module and enum globs use their respective child lookup. symbol/mod.rs supplies per-kind namespaces and external-child dispatch; scope.rs supplies ancestry and edition-specific prelude names. ribs.rs searches scopes and entries in reverse order. expr.rs clones block scope and pushes/pops ribs; infer_ctx.rs allocates body-global LocalIds and stores types by ID in each cloned scope, preserving sparse IDs and restored outer bindings. uses.rs now separately audits expansion-sensitive relative import roots after expansion. Generated binding provenance is determined on the binding item (including use declarations), rather than the eventual definition. Anchored imports are exempt, source-written bindings retain precedence, identical definitions do not conflict, and the in-flight root prevents self-rediscovery through cyclic routes. The captured span and local module helper fragments establish generated/file provenance and local-item conversion; the dedicated expansion_import_ambiguity anchor owns the detailed new algorithm contract and its larger test matrix.

Test adequacy: local_shadowing_does_not_change_qualified_lookup and qualified_paths_select_the_named_module_scope assert exact definition identities despite same types and a shadowing local. nested_scope_shadowing_restores_the_outer_binding and sibling_scopes_do_not_share_bindings_or_local_type_slots assert both identity and distinct bool/u8/u16 types across scope boundaries. explicit_imports_take_precedence_over_globs covers aliases and named imports; direct_items_take_precedence_over_globs covers direct definitions; named_type_import_takes_precedence_over_the_standard_prelude covers Type namespace priority. type_value_and_macro_namespaces_are_independent checks coexistence of type/function/bang macro names and a generated callable item. absolute_external_paths_bypass_a_shadowing_local_module distinguishes local and external symbols. transitive_cyclic_globs_resolve_a_value_definition and the library transitive_local_globs_resolve_and_glob_cycles_terminate check successful transitive resolution and finite missing-name lookup through a cycle. repeated_glob_routes_to_one_definition_are_unambiguous asserts deduplication, while competing_glob_definitions_remain_ambiguous_despite_equal_types requires a diagnostic and unresolved symbol. enum_glob_import_resolves_a_variant and external_enum_glob_import_resolves_a_variant cover both enum sources. Four edition tests assert TryInto availability in 2021 and absence in 2018, and IntoFuture availability in 2024 and absence in 2021. The three associated macro_glob_paths tests require an error for the generated competing import root even when unused, and require successful checking for explicitly qualified and directly source-written controls. The harness preparation code was captured and inspected: it runs rustc independently and requires both compiler results before returning observations; these compile fixtures therefore provide differential diagnostic evidence in addition to Sage snapshots.

Remaining deferral: semantic_spec::todo::resolution_lookup_precedence explicitly retains macro subnamespace distinctions and Rust2015 path rules. This is justified remaining work requiring corresponding fixtures and semantics, not executable evidence. No N/A entries exist. The new regression does not replace or erase that TODO. A normal-only import audit would miss the generated-root regression; treating every named binding as generated would fail the source-written control; ignoring path anchors would fail the qualified control. These meaningful positive/negative assertions address the changed behavior.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test lookup_precedence --test macro_glob_paths with snapshot updating disabled: 18 and 10 tests passed respectively. The pre-existing library test was inspected but not rerun separately by this reviewer. No production or test files were modified by this review. No additional edits requested.
